# Mike Holp: AI Automation Station

Mike Holp tests new AI models, agents, and automation tools on real builds and publishes the results on the AI Automation Station YouTube channel. Most videos cover Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and n8n, with every setup step shown. He also builds TubeAnalytics and VisiScan and hosts AI Income Lab, the paid learning community on Skool.

AI Income Lab here means "AI Income Lab by Mike Holp" (skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346). It is not affiliated with other Skool groups or courses that use a similar name.

## Key facts

- Product and membership facts reviewed November 8, 2026 against the published site. Check the linked official pages for subsequent changes.
- New long-form videos most days; the full archive is at /videos.
- TubeAnalytics: YouTube analytics for creators, currently temporarily unavailable. No active trial or subscription offer is advertised on this site.
- VisiScan: checks whether AI assistants recommend a business. Free scan with no signup; full report $49 USD once; weekly monitoring from $29 USD a month.
- AI Income Lab: Skool community with 2,900+ members. Standard $29, Premium $49, VIP $89 a month, or $290, $490, $890 a year. VIP adds weekly live group coaching and Q&A, software deals, and 6,400+ n8n templates. Coaching is group learning support. Custom business implementation is separate and is not included in membership. Ask about project scope before joining.
- AI Income Lab billing is in USD. Free written guides and videos are separate from the paid Skool membership; automation hosting, AI API usage, and other software can cost extra.
- On Standard, Beginner’s Automation Course unlocks at Skool level 2 and VAPI AI Voice Agent Course at level 4. Premium and VIP include immediate access to both and the Complete AI Avatar Video Course.
- Income is not guaranteed; results depend on the project, experience, and time invested.
- Sponsorship: brands can sponsor a build shown on the channel. Dedicated video $1,500, YouTube Short $400, LinkedIn post $350, AI Income Lab post $300, or all four as a campaign for $2,250 ($2,550 separately). Past sponsored builds include Treg, DataForSEO, BrowserAct, Bluehost and Apify.

- [Build a Chat Web App in Google AI Studio, No Code](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/google-ai-studio-chat-app.html): Build a ChatGPT-style web app in Google AI Studio build mode, connect the OpenAI API, then see what deploying needs. Notes from an October 2025 recording.
- [OpenCode Stripe Billing Build: A SaaS Case Study](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-stripe-billing-saas.html): Watch OpenCode add Stripe subscription pages to a SaaS app, fix a Prisma and missing-dependency build, and see what was not tested.
- [n8n Social Post Template: Trends, Research, Posting](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/n8n-social-media-agent-template.html): Import n8n’s multi-social post template, test the Google Trends and keyword steps, and see why the Perplexity and posting steps still failed.
- [n8n WhatsApp AI agent setup guide](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/n8n-whatsapp-ai-agent.html): Build the two-part n8n WhatsApp reply workflow: the trigger, an AI agent on OpenRouter, the Meta app setup, and the verification error left unresolved.
- [Make.com Course: Sheets, OpenAI, Airtable, Facebook](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-com-beginner-course-scenarios.html): Follow a Make.com beginner course: a Sheets to Gmail template, an OpenAI, Airtable and Facebook scenario with its errors, and an Apollo lead scraper.
- [Make.com business automation examples](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-business-automation-examples.html): Make.com business automations from one recording: an email reply, community members to an email list, Messenger, Instagram, cold email and lead scraping.
- [ChatGPT Thumbnails: Audit CTR and Redesign](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/chatgpt-thumbnail-ctr-pipeline.html): Audit channel thumbnail CTR, note brightness and contrast targets from the recording, then run the master prompt in ChatGPT Images.

# Pricing: AI Income Lab by Mike Holp

Reviewed November 12, 2026. AI Income Lab is the paid learning community on Skool (skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346). Prices are in USD and are charged by Skool. This site never sees payment details. Check the Skool plans page for current prices: https://www.skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346/plans

## Plans

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | $29 | $290 | Self-directed learners building their first workflows and unlocking lessons as they participate |
| Premium | $49 | $490 | Builders ready to make automations, voice agents and avatar videos with immediate course access |
| VIP | $89 | $890 | Builders who want weekly group help with their projects and reusable n8n workflows |

Cancel before the next billing period from your Skool account.

## What each plan includes

- Standard: community, courses and tutorials; Beginner's Automation Course (unlocks at Skool level 2); VAPI AI Voice Agent Course (unlocks at level 4).
- Premium: everything in Standard, immediate access to the Beginner's Automation Course and the VAPI AI Voice Agent Course, and the Complete AI Avatar Video Course.
- VIP: everything in Premium, weekly live group coaching and Q&A, the Ultimate N8N Template Library (6,400+ workflows), and software deals.

## Limits and scope

- Coaching is weekly group coaching and Q&A for members implementing what they learn. Custom business implementation is separate and is not included in membership. Ask about project scope before joining.
- No income is guaranteed.

## Free without joining

All written guides (https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides.html) and YouTube videos are free and need no Skool login. The tools used in the guides may need their own accounts or charge for usage.

## Other products by Mike Holp

- VisiScan (https://visiscan.app): free scan with no signup; full report $49 once; weekly monitoring from $29 a month.
- TubeAnalytics: currently temporarily unavailable. No trial or subscription is offered on this site.

## Every written guide, with its quick answer

### 9Router Cost Tracking: Combos and Fallbacks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/9router-cost-tracking-fallbacks.html (updated 2026-11-14)
On 9 July 2026, 9Router ran as a local proxy so OpenCode token use and estimated cost stayed visible, with model combos, auto-fallback from subscription to cheap to free, and weekly quota on the same dashboard. Install is on the 9Router setup guide.

### 9Router setup and update command
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/9router-setup.html (updated 2026-11-14)
9Router is a gateway between your coding tools and their model providers. It gives Claude Code, Codex and similar tools one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, http://localhost:20128/v1, plus a dashboard for providers, keys, model combos and usage. Install it with npm install -g 9router, add one provider and verify one request before adding fallbacks. The default port is 20128; start it with 9router --port 8080 to change it. The CLI checks for updates each time it starts, and Docker users update with docker pull decolua/9router:latest.

### How does agentic AI differ from traditional automation?
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/agentic-ai-vs-traditional-automation.html (updated 2026-11-13)
Traditional automation follows a path you drew in advance. Agentic AI is handed a goal and a set of tools, and it decides which steps to take. That difference changes how you build, test and trust the system.

### AI agent workflow: choose tools, add checks, keep control
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-agent-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-14)
an agent workflow uses a model to choose among steps or tools toward a goal. Start with one bounded task, give it only the tools and data needed, validate its output, and require approval before it sends messages, changes records, spends money or publishes content.

### AI automation agency: sell services to small businesses
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-automation-services-small-business.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Sell one recurring task as a fixed deliverable. Run discovery first, agree acceptance checks before you build, make the record flow work before adding any AI step, price on effort, scope and value, and hand over documentation with a maintenance plan. Skip vague “AI transformation” offers: neither you nor the owner can tell when they are finished.

### What Is AI Automation? Examples, Tools and a First Build
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-automation.html (updated 2026-11-11)
AI automation combines rules-based automation with an AI step that classifies, extracts, drafts or decides inside a workflow, so an incoming event can become a checked result and a useful action without someone manually copying information between every stage of the process.

### AI content creation workflow: images, video and audio
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-content-creation-workflows.html (updated 2026-11-14)
use AI to draft or transform content, then review every output before publishing. Start with the audience and format, prepare the source material, generate one small draft, check accuracy and rights, and export only after a person approves it.

### AI side hustles for beginners: 7 services to test
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-side-hustles.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Pick a small service whose output you can check yourself: lead intake, follow-up drafts, recurring reports, spreadsheet cleanup, FAQ drafts, specialist editing or workflow documentation. Judge each by the skill it needs, its startup cost and the time to a first client, then test the closest one this week before paying for tools. None of these are earnings claims.

### AI Rocket Demo: Three.js Scene and Camera Controls
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-threejs-rocket-demo.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Start from a source prompt you can read, generate a single-file rocket scene, inspect the HTML preview, then add zoom and rotation. The original prompt is not reproduced here. What I built is a visual coding exercise, not a physics-validated simulator, and the camera controls are the part you can learn from and reuse.

### Token Usage Dashboard: ccusage, RTK and Costs
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-token-usage-dashboard.html (updated 2026-11-14)
On 3 August 2026, ccusage was installed with the npx quick start, then a local Python dashboard showed daily, weekly and monthly token use. RTK showed 35 million tokens saved. Those figures are from that recording, not a live invoice.

### AI Visibility Tracker: SaaS Build Log
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-visibility-tracker-saas-build.html (updated 2026-11-12)
This is a 6 July 2026 build log of Beacon, an MVP AI visibility tracker. The recording shows a landing page, Clerk login, a dashboard of metrics that were not interactive yet, DataForSEO live data, GEO bot files and a Stripe pricing page draft. It did not show a launched product or revenue.

### Apify agent skills setup in Cursor
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/apify-agent-skills.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Install the Apify agent skills with npx skills add apify/agent-skills, add your Apify API token to a .env file as APIFY_TOKEN, and run the lead generation skill from OpenCode in Cursor. In the 5 February 2026 recording, a Google Maps scrape of AI startups in San Francisco wrote 74 leads to a CSV with names and websites but no emails, so a second contact info scrape pulled emails from those sites into another CSV. The same install command can be used in Claude Code, though that path was described, not shown end to end.

### Build apps with AI coding agents: a safe first workflow
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/build-apps-with-ai-coding-agents.html (updated 2026-11-14)
give a coding agent one testable feature at a time. First inspect the project and write down the expected behavior. Let the agent propose a small change, review the files it touched, run the project's checks and compare the result with the requirement before adding another feature.

### ChatGPT Image Editing: Sketch-to-Scene and Local Edits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/chatgpt-images-sketch-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Sketch a scene, generate the image, then make one local edit and look over the whole result. In my test a rough sketch of two windows, a chair and a pet came back in the right layout in about 25 seconds, and marking a spot and asking for a dog added one there. Check placement, reference fidelity and anything that changed without being asked.

### How to use ChatGPT on Linux: web and desktop options
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/chatgpt-linux.html (updated 2026-11-14)
start with chatgpt.com in your browser. For a desktop install, follow OpenAI’s current Linux preview requirements and official download links. First try the fictional exercise below before using private material.

### ChatGPT Pro 20x vs 5x vs Plus: 2026 Limits and Codex Credits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/chatgpt-pro-20x.html (updated 2026-11-11)
as of October 31, 2026, ChatGPT Pro 20x (Pro 200) is available again at $200/month, and every Pro 200 subscription now gets the same, higher Work and Codex allowance.

### ChatGPT Thumbnails: Audit CTR and Redesign
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/chatgpt-thumbnail-ctr-pipeline.html (updated 2026-11-12)
Export YouTube Studio and YouTube Data API fields, score thumbnails on brightness, saturation, contrast, edge density, color, faces and keywords, then paste a master prompt into ChatGPT Images with the image. The 24 July 2026 recording showed a master prompt on screen. The caption track does not include that text, so this page does not reconstruct it. Correlation numbers below are what the recording showed, not a measured lift after the redesign.

### How to choose an AI model for a task
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/choosing-ai-models-for-a-task.html (updated 2026-11-07)
choose a model by testing it on representative examples of your actual task. Compare correct results, time, cost, privacy requirements and how safely it handles unclear input. A leaderboard or launch demo can help create a shortlist, but it cannot select a model for your own workflow.

### Claude Code tutorial: install and first task
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-code-for-beginners.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Claude Code is Anthropic’s coding agent: it reads your project files, edits code and runs commands from the terminal. It is included in paid Claude plans, starting with Pro at $20 a month. Install it with Anthropic’s native installer, sign in with your subscription account, then ask it to explain one project and make one small change you can inspect.

### Claude Code Second Brain: Cortex Project Tour
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-code-second-brain.html (updated 2026-11-12)
Cortex is a personal Claude Code project that stores business notes in markdown, adds a Radar view and a theme graph, and pulls tools such as VidIQ over MCP. The 17 July 2026 recording is a tour. It is not an installable product, and the LeadScope prompt text was not spoken.

### Claude Code Task Manager: Scope, Checks and Packaging
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-code-task-manager.html (updated 2026-11-11)
I built a Windows and Linux task manager in Claude Code in about three hours by asking a chat model for a detailed build prompt, then checking the numbers against another system monitor. Start with a small brief, verify each metric against a tool you trust, and only package the app once the values hold up. The source is on GitHub if you would rather build my version than prompt your own.

### Claude Code Video Editor Skill: Build and Run
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-code-video-editor-skill.html (updated 2026-11-14)
In the 15 July 2026 recording, a custom long-form video-editor skill for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode transcribes clips with Whisper, picks a hook and segments, then exports a 1080p 30 fps MP4 plus a chapters file. Optimize it with a detailed prompt, approve the guardrail phases, and run the spoken command on the files in the working directory.

### Codex vs Claude Code: how I use both and route tasks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-code-vs-codex.html (updated 2026-11-12)
Claude Code and Codex are both terminal coding agents. I use both and send each task to the tool that suits it. That is my own working arrangement, not a benchmark.

### Claude Fable 5 Games: Prompts and Plugins
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-fable-5-game-prompts.html (updated 2026-11-14)
The 3 July 2026 recording uses Claude Fable 5 on a small island-game example, then shows effort modes, plan mode, on-screen prompt briefs and the Compound Engineering plugin. The YouTube title says games in seconds. This page only repeats what that session actually ran, not a guaranteed build time.

### Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku vs Fable: which to use
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-models-compared.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Use Claude Opus 5.5 for most coding and agent work: it is Anthropic’s recommended starting point and costs $4 / $20 per million input / output tokens. Use Sonnet 5.5 ($2 / $10) when speed and cost matter more, for well-scoped fixes and frequent coding turns. Use Haiku 5.5 (from $0.10 / $0.50) for high-volume jobs such as classification, extraction and sub-agents. Keep Fable 5.1 ($10 / $50) for the hardest long-running tasks, after Opus 5.5 at a higher effort has fallen short.

### CleanYourTV with Claude Code: TCL Setup and Risks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/cleanyourtv-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Check that your TV runs Android TV or Google TV, turn on USB debugging, paste the CleanYourTV prompt into Claude Code and let it back up the TV before it changes anything. On my TCL it disabled the apps I don't use and installed a much cleaner, faster home screen, but several remote buttons stopped working. Keep the restore command handy and test every button before you call it done.

### Codex CLI install: Mac, Windows and Linux
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-cli.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Codex CLI is OpenAI’s coding agent for the terminal. On Mac or Linux, install it with curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh. On Windows, use the PowerShell installer below. npm (npm install -g @openai/codex) and Homebrew also work. Then run codex in a project folder and choose Sign in with ChatGPT.

### Codex on Linux: desktop app and Linux setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-on-linux.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Install OpenAI’s Codex desktop preview on a supported Linux distribution, then sign in with ChatGPT. For the terminal CLI on Mac, Windows or Linux, follow the Codex CLI install guide.

### Internal Link Audit with Codex: A Reviewed SEO Workflow
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-seo-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Give Codex the research you want to apply, ask it to audit your site against that research, and have it write the findings to a report. Turn the report into a phased implementation plan saved in your repo, run the plan with a capable model, then ask Codex to run the same audit again. Review the diff before you deploy. The same loop works for most on-page SEO jobs. In this guide I use internal linking as the example.

### Codex usage limits by ChatGPT plan
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-usage-limits.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Codex usage limits depend on your plan and workload. Check Settings → Usage or /status in the CLI for remaining allowance and reset times, then use the continuation options available to your account (OpenAI guidance).

### Codex tutorial: make and verify a small code change
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Give Codex a narrow brief for one change, inspect the diff it proposes, then run a check that proves the change works. In this exercise you add a malformed-JSON request to a local API example and assert that it returns HTTP 400. You need Git, Node.js 22 or later and a configured coding assistant, but no provider key.

### React consent tracking: Google Analytics and Meta
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/consent-tracking.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Ask visitors for a clear choice, store the preference, and route every optional Google Analytics or Meta event through one consent guard so nothing fires before they accept. Give each event a single meaning: an outbound click shows interest, not a sale. Then test that declining keeps every optional tracker off.

A dashboard sample, a marketplace listing or a pushed commit is not the same as measured uplift in AI answers.

DataForSEO charges per API request, so check its current pricing and what each call costs before you build a larger workflow.

### DeepSeek Harness First Test: Setup Errors and Demo Limits

### Test your first AI API request locally
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/first-api-request.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Run a local test before calling a real provider: send one request to the example mock server, read the status code, and assert the result. A wrong key should return 401, an unknown model 404 and a valid request 200. The example needs Node.js 22 or later, costs nothing and never reads your API keys.

### Ghostty Config on Debian: Themes and Reload Checks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ghostty-debian-configuration.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Use current distro docs to install Ghostty, put your settings in ~/.config/ghostty/config.ghostty as key = value lines, then reload with Ctrl+Shift+, and open a fresh window to confirm. The memory numbers I saw against Konsole come from one session on my laptop, not a benchmark.

### Slow GrokBot credit drain: routines and caps

The steps below are the Maestro article settings shown in the 10 November 2026 recording, not a current billing quote.

### GrokBot for Beginners: First Bot, Access and Approvals
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-for-beginners.html (updated 2026-11-14)
GrokBot gives you AI "bots" that work like teammates. Bots share one persistent Linux box with separate agent desktops and browsers, can run in the background while your laptop is closed, and can save a workflow as a routine. To start, install the app, create one bot with a narrow job, connect only the apps it needs, require explicit approval for anything that sends or posts, and turn the task into a routine once it works twice.

### GrokBot for SEO: Audit Bots, Data and Reviewed Fixes
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-for-seo.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Import a site audit bot and an SEO bot from the GrokBot marketplace, give them your domain, and let them set up recurring audits as routines. Connect a keyword data source, such as Treg or a plugin like Ahrefs, so the bots work from real search data. Then ask for a full audit and a content plan, and send the fixes to a coding agent with a review step before anything ships.

### GrokBot job application agent setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-job-application-agent.html (updated 2026-11-14)
In GrokBot, talk to a Chief of Staff bot. Upload a resume, let a job-app agent pull matching roles, attach the reviewed resume to queued drafts, and keep outbound applications for your approval. This recording queued work for a later send window. It did not show a live send.

### GrokBot Virtual Office: Build a Custom Agent Dashboard
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-virtual-office.html (updated 2026-11-11)
A virtual office is a visual dashboard that shows every bot you run, what each one is doing and which tasks wait for your approval. I built mine in GrokBot by asking my chief of staff bot to create a Page. It shows active, finished and waiting tasks, an event log and a review handoff control for the selected bot, not a native one-click authorization mechanism. You build it the same way: describe the dashboard in plain language, then fix it one request at a time.

### GrokBot vs Dots: Onboarding, Job Drafts and Permissions
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-vs-dots.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Both support delegated cloud work, but do not assume the same computer or permission model. In the current GrokBot environment, agents share a persistent Linux box with separate desktops. Dots documentation describes a separate cloud computer for the dot. Dots is accessed through ChatGPT, with availability dependent on the documented plan, region and rollout conditions. GrokBot is xAI's bot app on desktop and iOS, where you can run many bots side by side. In my one head-to-head test, building a job application agent, GrokBot set up a working pipeline in minutes, while my dot took around 45 minutes and could not find contact emails. Try both on your own task before you decide.

### Herdr Desktop Guide: Setup, Workspaces and Limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/herdr-desktop-app.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Install the current official Herdr desktop app, open one repository as a space, and run agents in separate tabs. Closing the window is not the same as stopping herdr-core. The memory figure I saw in my video is one reading on my machine, not a benchmark.

### Herdr Terminal Guide: Workspaces and Coding-Agent Sessions
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/herdr-guide.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Herdr is a free, open source terminal workspace for coding agents. It does not replace Claude Code or Codex. It runs them in panes and tabs, groups them by project, keeps them running in a background server when you close the window, and marks each pane as working, blocked or idle. Install it with curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh, then run herdr in your project folder.

Copy the Windows PowerShell line from the Herdr download page, paste a gallery agent prompt to install a mod, then switch the layout to main-plus-insights to open the token dashboard. The Linux desktop walkthrough stays on Herdr desktop.

### HeyGen AI avatar tutorial: create your first video

### How to install OpenClaw: local, VPS or hosted, safely
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/install-openclaw.html (updated 2026-11-07)
Run OpenClaw on a VPS, a spare machine or a hosted service rather than your main computer. It can read files and run commands with your account’s permissions. Install it with the official installer: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash on macOS, Linux or WSL2, or iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex in Windows PowerShell. The installer sets up Node.js if needed and starts onboarding. Keep the gateway on localhost, and run openclaw security audit before you connect any accounts.

### Jev AI with Coding Agents: Skills, Access and Routed Tests
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/jev-skills-router-setup.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Jev is TypeSafe's model for fast, structured decisions, not a chat model for your coding agent. I installed the TypeSafe skill, hit a browser-skill failure that turned out to be a missing API key, then ran Codex through a community router. Confirm real requests in the TypeSafe console before trusting any setup.

### Kilo Code tutorial: install, free models and first task
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/kilo-code-tutorial.html (updated 2026-11-08)
Kilo Code is an open-source AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal. Install the VS Code extension (choose Install Pre-Release Version) or run npm install -g @kilocode/cli, sign in with a free Kilo account, and pick a model. You can use free models through Auto Free, your own API keys, local models, or paid credits. The software is free for individuals; model usage is billed separately. Before your first task, check which actions it may run without asking.

### Lovable vs Base44 vs Replit: pricing and which to pick
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/lovable-vs-base44-vs-replit.html (updated 2026-11-08)
Pick Lovable for a polished website or front end you want live quickly; Pro starts at $25 a month for 100 credits. Pick Base44 for a simple internal app with sign-in and a database built in; paid plans start at $16 a month billed yearly. Pick Replit if you want a full coding workspace and expect to edit the code yourself; Core is $20 a month with $20 of usage included. All three have a free plan that is enough to build a first version, not to run it for real users.

### Make.com business automation examples
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-business-automation-examples.html (updated 2026-11-14)
The recording walks through about ten of the speaker’s own Make.com scenarios: an email auto-responder, Skool members into an email list, a Messenger bot, an Instagram comment reply, a Google Sheets cold-email sender, an Apollo lead scraper, YouTube description and topic generators, and Make’s template library. Most are two to four modules. Treat the auto-reply and cold-email ones carefully, since consent and quality are not covered.

### Make.com Course: Sheets, OpenAI, Airtable, Facebook
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-com-beginner-course-scenarios.html (updated 2026-11-12)
The recording is a Make.com beginner course in lessons: a tour of the dashboard, a template that emails a Gmail message for each new Google Sheet row, a scenario built from scratch with OpenAI, Airtable, an image model and a Facebook post, and an Apollo lead scraper through Apify that writes to Google Sheets. Errors are left in on purpose, which makes it a useful guide to fixing scenarios.

### Make.com Google Sheets tutorial: filter approved requests
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-first-automation.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Create a Make.com scenario that watches new rows in an Intake sheet, filters for Approved = yes, and adds each approved row to a Work queue tab. Run it once on two fictional test rows: the approved one should arrive and the rejected one should not. Keep the schedule off until both checks pass.

### How to make money with AI fast: the honest path
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-ai-fast.html (updated 2026-11-14)
there is no dependable fast way to make money with AI. AI makes drafts quick, but income comes from finding a person who wants the result, trusts you to check it and agrees to pay, and that part does not speed up because the tool did. The fastest honest route: pick a task you can check yourself, ask one person who has that task, and deliver one small result.

### Make money with AI with no experience
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-ai-no-experience.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Start with a task you already understand, such as organizing requests or cleaning a spreadsheet. Build the smallest version on free tiers, without AI first, use it on your own work, then offer the narrow version to one person you know. AI helps with parts of the job; customers still pay for your judgment and reliability, and income is not guaranteed.

### Make money with ChatGPT: 4 client services
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-chatgpt.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Use ChatGPT inside client work you can check yourself: editing documents, research summaries with sources, customer FAQ drafts from approved information, or bounded custom GPT projects. Define the finished deliverable first, review every output before handing it over, and agree on AI use and disclosure with the client. More output is not more value.

n8n publishes its source under its own fair-code licenses, which is not the same as an OSI open-source license. This guide lists five open-source tools for similar jobs and links each license file.

### OpenCode Go: pricing, models, limits and setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-go.html (updated 2026-11-14)
OpenCode Go is a monthly subscription to a curated set of open and low-cost coding models, run by the team behind OpenCode. Go costs $10 a month, Go Plus $40 a month, and Go Teams $20 per member per month. Each model has its own monthly allowance in dollars, with 20% usable per 5 hours and 50% per week. You connect it in OpenCode with /connect, then pick a model with /models. It is optional: OpenCode itself is free and works with other providers.

### OpenCode SEO Audit Skills: Site Checks and Files
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-seo-audit-skills.html (updated 2026-11-12)
In OpenCode, type /skills, run an SEO audit skill on a live site, and let it work on llms.txt, ai.txt and sitemap.xml. This recording audited visiscan.app on 4 August 2026 and showed DeepSeek V4 Pro usage already at 98% of the month. Plan signup is on the OpenCode Go guide, not here.

### OpenCode Stripe Billing Build: A SaaS Case Study
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-stripe-billing-saas.html (updated 2026-11-12)
The recording pasted one billing prompt into OpenCode, which added Stripe subscription models, a pricing page, a billing invoices page, a checkout success page and an environment setup file. The build then failed twice and OpenCode fixed it by regenerating the Prisma client and installing the missing Stripe packages. No real payment was tested.

### OpenCode vs Claude Code: pricing, setup and limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-vs-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-11)
pick Claude Code if you already pay for a Claude plan and want Anthropic’s own coding agent. Pick OpenCode if you want an MIT-licensed, open source agent that can use models from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or local options such as Ollama. Neither is ranked faster here: run the same small task in both and compare setup time, failed requests and the final diff.

### OpenDesign (Open Design) on Linux: Source Setup and Slides
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opendesign-linux-slides.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Follow the recorded Linux source setup, make one first design, then export a standalone HTML deck. On Linux that means cloning the official repo, using Node 24 with Corepack, then running pnpm tools-dev run web. Local agents, BYOK keys and hosted credits are billed separately, so a free desktop app is not free inference.

### OpenRouter setup: API key and free models
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/openrouter-setup.html (updated 2026-11-14)
OpenRouter is one API in front of hundreds of models from many providers. Create an account, add credits if you need paid models, and create an API key at openrouter.ai/settings/keys. Then point any OpenAI-compatible tool at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with that key. Free models end in :free and are capped at 50 requests a day, or 1,000 a day once you have bought at least 10 credits. Paid models cost the provider’s listed price; OpenRouter charges a 5.5% fee when you buy credits.

### OpenSEO review: setup, data costs and practical limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/openseo-review.html (updated 2026-11-11)
OpenSEO is worth evaluating for focused SEO research, but its free self-hosted app still needs paid data, and my demo doesn't show it replacing every paid suite.

In Rank Prompt, enter a site, run a visibility scan, pick categories so the product can generate prompts, then read where those prompts show up across the models you selected. The 12 November 2026 recording then installed the Rank Prompt MCP in Claude Code, authenticated with an API key, and used that data to edit pages and draft outreach. Rank Prompt sponsored this video. The on-site edits were not treated as an instant rank change.

### RTK Token Savings: Install, Hooks and Checks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/rtk-token-savings-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Install RTK from GitHub with the curl line on that page or with brew install rtk, add it to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, run rtk init so the hook is present, then run rtk gain to read savings. On 21 July 2026, GLM 5.2 showed 169,000 tokens saved.

### GrokBot WordPress Workflow: Long-Form Videos to Drafts
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/run-a-blog-with-grokbot.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Locate the WordPress connector through the app’s supported connection flow. In my video the panel is called Plugins. Connect only the permissions needed for your approved task. Create a blog writer bot and give it a source, such as your YouTube videos. In my video, the bot retrieves transcripts and prepares posts, excerpts, categories and tags, with some items scheduled. For a new setup, request reviewable drafts rather than assuming publication is authorized. Keep the initial workflow draft-only. Scheduling and any subscriber email are separate approvals, not a default result of asking for an article.

### Self-host n8n on Ubuntu: Docker and Node.js setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/self-host-n8n.html (updated 2026-11-14)
For a machine that stays on, use Docker or Docker Compose, which n8n’s docs recommend. npm installs are deprecated from n8n 3.0. The recorded Ubuntu video uses Node.js 24 and npm install n8n -g, which still works for learning on a laptop. Either way, open localhost:5678, create the owner account, and run a three-node test workflow before adding credentials. Self-hosting is free, and this setup is reachable only from your own computer.

### Trakkr and Codex: AI Visibility, Crawlers and Visits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/trakkr-codex-visibility-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Connect Trakkr's hosted MCP server to Codex, pull the action list into a report, and read it before you let Codex edit anything. Keep AI visibility, crawler visits, citations and real visitors as separate numbers. An assistant naming your brand is not a click, and a fix list is not a result.

### Treg in GrokBot: Connect Data Tools and Control Costs
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/treg-inside-grokbot.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Treg is a catalog of external APIs that an agent reaches through one connection and one token. To use it in GrokBot, open Plugins in the left sidebar, search for "treg," add it, and sign in. Your bots can then search the catalog by task, see the price of each endpoint, and make the call. You pay per call from a prepaid balance, or connect your own API keys for providers you already pay for.

### Vapi AI tutorial: build a voice agent, test calls, webhooks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/vapi-voice-agent-tutorial.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Vapi is a platform for building voice AI agents: a transcriber turns the caller’s speech into text, a model writes the reply and a voice speaks it. To build one, create an assistant with a first message and system prompt, test it in the dashboard, connect a phone number, then confirm webhook events arrive before adding business actions.

### VisiScan AI Visibility: Free Scan and Report
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/visiscan-ai-visibility-audit.html (updated 2026-11-12)
Enter a domain in VisiScan, run the free scan, and read the readiness and visibility scores. The 22 July 2026 recording also opened sitemap, robots.txt and machine-readable file checks, then showed a paid full report generated in Codex. VisiScan is Mike Holp's own product.

### What is an AI agent? Definition, examples and first build
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent.html (updated 2026-11-11)
An AI agent is software that uses a language model and a set of tools to work toward a goal, choosing its own next step after each result. A workflow follows steps you wrote in advance. Use an agent when the steps cannot be planned ahead, and add checks before it acts.

### What is MCP? The Model Context Protocol explained
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-mcp.html (updated 2026-11-11)
MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard for connecting AI apps to outside tools and data. An app such as Claude Code or Codex connects to MCP servers, and each server offers tools the model can call. Anthropic open-sourced it in November 2024, and ChatGPT, VS Code and Cursor support it too.

### What is n8n used for? Real uses and a first workflow
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-n8n-used-for.html (updated 2026-11-08)
n8n is a workflow automation tool. You connect apps, APIs and AI models on a visual canvas, and n8n runs the steps when something happens. This guide lists jobs people hand to it and a first workflow you can check.

### YouTube channel growth workflow: research, publish, learn
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-channel-growth-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-14)
choose an idea for a specific viewer, make the title and thumbnail promise clear, publish a video that keeps that promise, then use several analytics signals to decide what to improve. A single view count or competitor estimate cannot tell you why a video performed as it did.

### React YouTube feed tutorial: API, caching and fallbacks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-feed.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Fetch your uploads on the server, keep a saved list as a fallback, and render that list into the HTML so the page still shows watch links and thumbnails when the YouTube request fails, then refresh it in the browser. Check the result by making the live fetch fail on purpose and confirming the videos still appear.
